title: Inductor mixed device operations not handled correctly, maybe buffer reuse problem?

labels.name: triaged
labels.description: This issue has been looked at a team member, and triaged and prioritized into an appropriate module

body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

```
    @torch._dynamo.config.patch(capture_scalar_outputs=True)
    def test_bitwise(self):
        def fn(x):
            full = torch.full((), 11)
            i0 = full.item()
            r = torch.full((i0,), 0)
            return x + r.sum()
    
        self.common(
            fn,
            (
                torch.randn(20),
            ),
        )
```

fails with device='cuda' with

```
  File "/data/users/ezyang/a/pytorch/torch/_inductor/compile_fx.py", line 649, in run
    return model(new_inputs)
  File "/data/users/ezyang/a/pytorch/torch/_inductor/codecache.py", line 852, in _run_from_cache
    return compiled_graph.compiled_artifact(inputs)
  File "/tmp/torchinductor_ezyang/cp/ccpvntaiovm2x7y6sarux4rfpvccskdrgonwufijplqnqnog2kpx.py", line 120, in call
    triton_poi_fused_add_2.run(arg0_1, buf2, buf3, 20, grid=grid(20), stream=stream0)
  File "/data/users/ezyang/a/pytorch/torch/_inductor/triton_heuristics.py", line 617, in run
    return launcher(
  File "<string>", line 7, in launcher
ValueError: Pointer argument (at 1) cannot be accessed from Triton (cpu tensor?)
```

The generated code is

```
def call(args):
    arg0_1, = args
    args.clear()
    assert_size_stride(arg0_1, (20, ), (1, ))
    buf0 = empty((), device='cpu', dtype=torch.int64)
    cpp_fused_full_0(buf0)
    u0 = buf0.item()
    buf1 = None
    buf2 = buf0; del buf0  # reuse
    cpp_fused_full_sum_1(buf2, u0)
    with torch.cuda._DeviceGuard(0):
        torch.cuda.set_device(0)
        buf3 = empty((20, ), device='cuda', dtype=torch.float32)
        # Source Nodes: [add], Original ATen: [aten.add]
        stream0 = get_raw_stream(0)
        triton_poi_fused_add_2.run(arg0_1, buf2, buf3, 20, grid=grid(20), stream=stream0)
        run_intermediate_hooks('add', buf3)
        del arg0_1
        return (buf3, )
```

You can see that buf2 = buf0 is a CPU buffer but it is passed straight to the Triton kernel. Maybe this is some sort of buffer reuse disaster?

### Versions

main, but you may need to patch in the stack at https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/118125 to have enough bugfixes to get this here
